paragraphs: We are one of the largest publicly-traded lodging real estate investment trusts ("REIT") with a diverse portfolio of iconic and market-leading hotels and resorts with significant underlying real estate value. As of February 20, 2026, our portfolio consists of 34 premium-branded hotels and resorts with approximately 23,000 rooms, located in prime United States ("U.S.") markets with high barriers to entry. Our strategic focus is on our 21 Core hotels, including one unconsolidated joint venture, with our consolidated Core hotels contributing approximately 90% of our Hotel Adjusted EBITDA. All of our rooms are located in the U.S. and its territories, and over 96% of rooms in our Core portfolio are luxury and upper upscale. We are focused on consistently delivering superior risk-adjusted returns to stockholders through active asset management and a thoughtful external growth strategy, with a strategic focus on our Core portfolio, while maintaining a strong and flexible balance sheet.

Park Intermediate Holdings LLC (our "Operating Company") directly or indirectly holds all of our assets and conducts all of our operations. We are structured as a traditional umbrella partnership REIT ("UPREIT"). Park Parent is the managing member of our Operating Company, and PK Domestic REIT Inc., a direct subsidiary of Park Parent, is a member of our Operating Company. We may, in the future, issue interests in (or from) our Operating Company in connection with acquiring hotels, financing, issuance of equity compensation or other purposes.

Our objective is to be the preeminent lodging REIT, focused on consistently delivering superior, risk-adjusted returns to stockholders through active asset management and a thoughtful external growth strategy, with a strategic focus on our Core portfolio, while maintaining a strong and flexible balance sheet. We intend to pursue our objective by divesting our Non-Core hotels to further enhance our overall portfolio quality and long-term growth profile, while utilizing sale proceeds to further reduce our leverage, re-invest in our Core portfolio and increase shareholder value, through the following strategies:

•Operational Excellence through Active Asset Management. We collaborate with our third-party managers to improve property-level operating performance and profitability for each of our hotels and resorts through our proactive asset management efforts. We continue to identify revenue-enhancement opportunities and drive cost efficiencies to maximize the operating performance, cash flow and value of each hotel. As a pure-play lodging real estate company with significant financial resources and an extensive portfolio of large, multi-use assets, including seven hotels (all within the Core portfolio) with 125,000 square feet of meeting space or more, we believe our ability to implement compelling return on investment initiatives represents a significant embedded growth opportunity, particularly for our Core portfolio. These may include the expansion of meeting platforms in convention and resort markets; the upgrade or redevelopment of existing amenities, including retail platforms, food and beverage outlets, pools and other facilities; the development of vacant land into income-generating uses, including retail or mixed-use properties; or the redevelopment or optimization of underutilized spaces. Recent and ongoing projects at our Core hotels include:

◦Completion of more than $220 million of projects at our Bonnet Creek complex in 2024, including a meeting space expansion project and renovation of guestrooms, existing meeting space, lobbies, the golf course and other recreational amenities;

◦Nearly $250 million of comprehensive guestroom renovations at the iconic Rainbow Tower at the Hilton Hawaiian Village Waikiki Beach Resort, the Palace Tower at the Hilton Waikoloa Village and the Main Tower at the Hilton New Orleans Riverside, which commenced in 2024:

▪Completed the first of three phases of guestroom renovations totaling $16 million at the main tower of the Hilton New Orleans Riverside in November 2024 and the second phase of over $30 million of guestroom renovations in January 2026, with the third phase expected to total approximately $37 million with a completion date in late 2026;

▪Completed the first of two phases of guestroom renovations and room conversions at our Hawaii hotels, totaling nearly $75 million, during the first quarter of 2025, with the second and final phase of guestroom renovations and room conversions at the Hilton Waikoloa Village
completed in January 2026 and the second and final phase at the Hilton Hawaiian Village Waikiki Beach Resort expected to be completed in March 2026 for approximately $85 million for both hotels; and

◦Over $100 million of comprehensive renovations at the Royal Palm South Beach Miami, a Tribute Portfolio Resort, which commenced in May 2025 and includes the full renovation of all 393 guestrooms at the oceanfront hotel, along with the addition of 11 new guestrooms, with an expected reopening in June 2026.

We also may create value through repositioning certain Core hotels across brands or chain scale segments and exploring adaptive reuse opportunities to ensure our assets achieve their highest and best use. Finally, we are focused on maintaining the competitive strength of our Core hotels and adapting to evolving customer preferences by renovating properties to provide updated guestroom design, open and activated lobby areas, food and beverage and public spaces, and modernized meeting space.

•Pursuing Growth and Diversification through Prudent Capital Allocation. We intend to leverage our scale, liquidity and transaction expertise to create value throughout all phases of the lodging cycle through opportunistic acquisitions, dispositions, and/or corporate transactions, in addition to value-enhancing return on investment projects at our Core hotels, which we believe will enable us to further diversify our portfolio. Since our spin-off on January 3, 2017 from Hilton Parent that established us as an independent, publicly traded company, we have sold or otherwise disposed of 51 hotels, most of them located in lower growth domestic and international markets for a total of $3 billion, which provided us with additional liquidity to de-leverage our balance sheet and to execute on a variety of strategic corporate initiatives. In addition, we continue to make progress to divest our remaining Non-Core hotels. We will continue to opportunistically seek to expand our presence in target markets and further diversify over time, including by acquiring hotels, when appropriate, that are affiliated with leading hotel brands and operators.

•Maintaining a Strong and Flexible Balance Sheet. We intend to maintain a strong and flexible balance sheet that will enable us to navigate the various seasons of the lodging cycle. We expect to maintain sufficient liquidity with minimal short-term maturities and intend to have a mix of debt that will provide us with the flexibility to prepay debt when desired, dispose of Non-Core hotels, pursue our value enhancement strategies within our existing Core portfolio, and support acquisition activity. In September 2025, the Company and our Operating Company entered into a Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the "Credit Agreement"), which provides for an increase in the aggregate commitments for the senior unsecured revolving credit facility ("Revolver") from $950 million to $1 billion, a new $800 million senior unsecured delayed draw term loan facility ("2025 Delayed Draw Term Loan"), which allows for up to three draws through September 17, 2026, and the continuation of the $200 million senior unsecured term loan ("2024 Term Loan"). The Credit Agreement includes the option to increase the Revolver and increase or add new term loans under the Credit Agreement by up to $1 billion in the aggregate, subject to obtaining additional lender commitments and the satisfaction of certain customary conditions. We expect to reduce our level of secured debt over time, as we intend to draw upon the 2025 Delayed Draw Term Loan in 2026 to assist in repaying two mortgage loans totaling approximately $1.4 billion maturing in 2026. We also intend to further pay down our debt with proceeds from the sales of our Non-Core hotels, which will provide additional balance sheet flexibility. Our senior management team has extensive experience managing capital structures over multiple lodging cycles and has extensive and long-standing relationships with numerous lending institutions and financial advisors to address our capital needs.

headings: We face various risks posed by our acquisition activities.
Contractual and other disagreements with or involving our current and future third-party hotel managers and franchisors could make us liable to them or result in litigation costs or other expenses.
We may be deemed to be a joint employer with our third-party hotel managers under certain new non-income tax laws, rules and regulations.

Cyber threats and the risk of cybersecurity incidents affecting our hotel managers' or our own information technology and systems, including third-party service providers, could materially adversely affect our business.
Costs associated with, or failure to maintain, brand operating standards may materially and adversely affect our results of operations and profitability.

If the insurance that we carry does not sufficiently cover damage or other potential losses or liabilities involving our properties, including as a result of terrorism and climate change, our profits could be reduced.
We have investments in joint venture projects, which limit our ability to manage third-party risks associated with these projects.

We depend on external sources of capital for future growth. Any disruption to our ability to access capital at times and on terms reasonably acceptable to us may adversely affect our business and results of operations.
We could be materially and adversely affected if we are found to be in breach of a ground lease or are unable to renew a ground lease.
We operate in a highly competitive industry.
The lodging industry is subject to seasonal volatility, which is expected to contribute to fluctuations in our financial condition and results of operations.
Governmental regulation may adversely affect the operation of our properties and our Company as a whole.
Risks Related to our REIT Status and Certain Other Tax Items
If we do not maintain our qualification as a REIT, we will be subject to tax as a C corporation and could face a substantial tax liability.
We may face other tax liabilities that reduce our cash flows.
Complying with REIT requirements may force us to borrow to make distributions to stockholders.
Our transactions with our TRSs may cause us to be subject to a 100% penalty tax on certain income or deductions if those transactions are not conducted on arm's-length terms.
If the leases of our hotels to our TRS lessees are not respected as true leases for U.S. federal income tax purposes, we will fail to qualify as a REIT.
paragraphs: Owning our common stock involves a number of significant risks. You should consider carefully the following risk factors. If any of the following risks, as well as additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial, occur, our business, liquidity, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. If this were to happen, the market price of our common stock could decline significantly, and you could lose all or a part of the value of your ownership in our common stock. In addition, the statements in the following risk factors include forward-looking statements. See "Forward-Looking Statements."

Economic disruptions, including the impact from inflation, elevated interest rates or an economic slowdown or recession, may adversely impact and disrupt, our business, financial performance and condition, operating results and cash flows.

Economic disruptions, including as a result of elevated interest rates and elevated rates of inflation or a potential economic slowdown or recession, may adversely affect our business by affecting consumer sentiment and demand for travel, which can cause fluctuations in hotel revenues or earnings at our hotels. Our labor or other costs may also rise due to inflation, and there can be no assurance that we will be able to pass cost increases on to travelers through higher rates. There can also be no assurances that we will not experience future fluctuations in hotel revenues or earnings at our hotels due to inflation and other macroeconomic factors, local economic factors and demand, a potential economic slowdown or a recession and geopolitical conflicts or trends, including trade policy, travel barriers or changes in travel preferences for U.S. destinations.

Additionally, the effects of the global COVID-19 pandemic on the hotel industry were unprecedented, and another pandemic or other unexpected event that results in a prolonged decrease in travel in the future could have similar affects, including a drastic reduction in global demand for lodging and historically low occupancy levels. These challenges may adversely impact and disrupt, our business, financial performance and condition, operating results and cash flows.

Other factors that would negatively impact our ability to successfully operate, or that could otherwise significantly adversely impact and disrupt our business, financial performance and condition, operating results and cash flows, include:

•sustained negative consumer or business sentiment, economic metrics (including inflation, unemployment levels, discretionary spending and declines in personal wealth) or demand for travel, which could further adversely impact demand for lodging;

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the accompanying consolidated financial statements, related notes included thereto and Item 1A., "Risk Factors," appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. For the discussion and analysis of our 2023 financial condition and results of operations compared to 2024, refer to Item 7., "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

We have a diverse portfolio of iconic and market-leading hotels and resorts with significant underlying real estate value. We currently have interests in 34 hotels consisting of premium-branded hotels and resorts with approximately 23,000 rooms, located in prime U.S. markets and its territories. Our strategic focus is on our Core portfolio, with our consolidated Core hotels contributing approximately 90% of our Hotel Adjusted EBITDA. Over 96% of rooms in our Core portfolio are luxury and upper upscale, and our Core hotels are located in major urban and convention areas, such as New York City, Washington, D.C., Chicago, Boston, New Orleans and Denver; and premier resorts in key leisure destinations, including Hawaii, Orlando, Key West and Miami Beach; as well as hotels in select airport and suburban locations.

Our objective is to be the preeminent lodging real estate investment trust ("REIT"), focused on consistently delivering superior, risk-adjusted returns to stockholders through active asset management and a thoughtful external growth strategy, while maintaining a strong and flexible balance sheet. As a pure-play real estate company with direct access to capital and independent financial resources, we believe our enhanced ability to implement compelling return on investment initiatives represents a significant embedded growth opportunity, particularly for our Core portfolio. Finally, given our scale and investment expertise, we believe we will be able to successfully execute single-asset and portfolio acquisitions and dispose of all 13 remaining Non-Core hotels to further enhance the value and diversification of our assets throughout the lodging cycle.

As a result of a shift in our business strategy to dispose of all Non-Core hotels, we now operate our business through three operating segments, our consolidated Core hotels, consolidated Non-Core hotels and unconsolidated hotels. Only our consolidated Core hotels and consolidated Non-Core hotels are reportable segments. Refer to Note 14: "Business Segment Information" in our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere within this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding our operating segments.

The consolidated financial statements reflect our financial position, results of operations and cash flows, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("U.S. GAAP"). Refer to Note 2: "Basis of Presentation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" in our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere within this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information.

Economic disruptions, including as a result of elevated interest and inflation rates, may adversely affect our business by affecting consumer sentiment and demand for travel. Heightened uncertainty due to ongoing changes to trade policy, tax policy and disruptions to government spending has resulted in inflationary concerns and changes in demand and travel preferences, which may affect the lodging industry. Additionally, geopolitical conflicts and trends may continue to decrease inbound international travel. During 2025, we relied on the performance of our hotels and active asset management to mitigate the effects of current macroeconomic uncertainty. While there can be no assurances that we will not experience further fluctuations in hotel revenues or earnings at our hotels due to inflation and other macroeconomic factors, local economic factors and demand, a potential economic slowdown or a recession, geopolitical conflicts or trends, disapproval of U.S. foreign or domestic policy, or another government shutdown, we are cautiously optimistic for 2026 based on upcoming major events, including the World Cup and the 250th anniversary of the U.S., continued benefits from transformative renovations at certain of our hotels, including the expected reopening of the Royal Palm South Beach Miami, a Tribute Portfolio Resort ("Royal Palm") in June 2026, the benefits of divesting Non-Core hotels and expected macroeconomic improvement from continued deregulation.

Revenues from our hotels are primarily derived from two categories of customers: transient and group, which historically have accounted for approximately two thirds and one third, respectively, of our rooms revenue. Transient guests are individual travelers who are traveling for business or leisure. Group guests are traveling for group events that reserve rooms for meetings, conferences or social functions sponsored by associations, corporate, social, military, educational, religious or other organizations. Group business usually includes a block of room accommodations, as well as other ancillary services, such as meeting facilities, catering and banquet services. A majority of our food and beverage sales and other ancillary services are provided to customers who also are occupying rooms at our hotels. As a result, occupancy affects all components of revenues from our hotels.
Rooms. Represents the sale of room rentals at our hotels and accounts for a substantial majority of our total revenue.

Food and beverage. Represents revenue from group functions, which may include both banquet revenue and audio and visual revenue, as well as revenue from outlets such as restaurants and lounges at our hotels.
Ancillary hotel. Represents revenue for guest services provided at our hotels, including parking, telecommunications, golf course and spa. Also includes tenant leases and other rental revenue.

Other. Primarily related to support services we provide to HGV timeshare properties that have a presence within or adjacent to certain of our hotels, which include cost reimbursements for the costs of providing housekeeping, landscaping, general maintenance and other services plus a fee representing a percentage of cost reimbursements.

Consumer demand. Consumer demand for our products and services is closely linked to the performance of the general economy and is sensitive to business and personal discretionary spending levels. Leading indicators of demand include gross domestic product, non-residential fixed investment and the consumer price index. Declines in consumer demand due to adverse general economic conditions, reductions in travel patterns, lower consumer confidence, outbreaks of pandemic or contagious diseases, and adverse political conditions can lower the revenues and profitability of our hotels. Further, competition for guests and the supply of services at our hotels affect our ability to sustain or increase rates charged to customers at our hotels. As a result, changes in consumer demand and general business cycles have historically subjected and could in the future subject our revenues to significant volatility. In addition, leisure travelers currently make up the majority of our transient demand. Therefore, we will be significantly more affected by trends in leisure travel than trends in business travel.

Supply. New room supply is an important factor that can affect the lodging industry's performance. Room rates and occupancy, and thus RevPAR, tend to increase when demand growth exceeds supply growth. The addition of new competitive hotels and resorts affects the ability of existing hotels and resorts to sustain or grow RevPAR, and thus profits. New development is determined largely by construction costs, the availability of financing and expected performance of existing hotels and resorts.
Rooms. These costs include housekeeping, reservation systems, room supplies, laundry services at our hotels and front desk costs.

paragraphs: 本公司為美國最大的上市旅館不動產投資信託（"REIT"）之一，擁有多元化的資產組合，包含許多知名且市場領先的旅館與度假村，並具有顯著的不動產價值。截至2026年2月20日，本公司資產組合包含34家高檔品牌旅館與度假村，約有23,000間客房，位於美國（"U.S.")主要市場，這些市場具有高進入門檻。本公司戰略重點為21家核心旅館，包括一家未合併的合資企業，其中本公司合併的核心旅館貢獻約90%的旅館調整後營運資金（Hotel Adjusted EBITDA）。所有客房均位於美國及其屬地，且本公司核心資產組閤中超過96%的客房為豪華與高檔旅館。本公司專注於透過積極的資產管理與深思熟慮的外部成長策略，持續為股東提供優越的風險調整後回報，同時維持強而有彈性的資產負債表。

Park Intermediate Holdings LLC（本公司之"營運公司"）直接或間接持有本公司所有資產，並執行本公司所有營運活動。本公司為傳統的傘型合夥REIT（"UPREIT"）。Park Parent為本公司營運公司的管理成員，而PK Domestic REIT Inc.為Park Parent的直接子公司，為本公司營運公司的成員。本公司未來可能因取得旅館、融資、發行股票報酬或其它用途，發行本公司營運公司的權益。
本公司目標為成為首屈一指的旅館REIT，專注於透過積極的資產管理與深思熟慮的外部成長策略，持續為股東提供優越的風險調整後回報，同時維持強而有彈性的資產負債表。本公司擬透過以下策略達成目標：

•透過積極資產管理實現運營卓越。本公司與第三方管理公司合作，透過積極的資產管理努力，提升各旅館與度假村的運營表現與獲利能力。本公司持續尋找收入提升機會，並推動成本效率，以最大化各旅館的運營表現、現金流與價值。作為一家純粹的旅館不動產公司，擁有顯著的財務資源與廣泛的大型多用途資產組合，包括七家旅館（全部為核心資產組合）擁有125,000平方英尺以上的會議空間，本公司相信我們實現有吸引力的投資回報計畫的能力，代表著重要的內生成長機會，特別是對我們的核心資產組合。這些計畫可能包括擴充會議空間於會議與度假市場；升級或重新開發現有設施，包括零售平台、餐飲設施、游泳池及其他設施；將閒置土地開發為產生收入的用途，包括零售或混合用途的不動產；或重新開發或優化未充分利用的空間。本公司核心旅館近期及持續進行的計畫包括：
◦2024年於Bonnet Creek複合體完成超過220百萬美元的計畫，包括會議空間擴建計畫與客房、現有會議空間、大廳、高爾夫球場及其他休閒設施的翻修；
◦於Hilton Hawaiian Village Waikiki Beach Resort的Rainbow Tower、Hilton Waikoloa Village的Palace Tower及Hilton New Orleans Riverside的Main Tower進行近250百萬美元的客房全面翻修，該計畫於2024年啟動：
▪於2024年11月完成Hilton New Orleans Riverside Main Tower第一階段客房翻修計畫，總計16百萬美元，並於2026年1月完成第二階段超過30百萬美元的客房翻修計畫，第三階段預計總計約37百萬美元，預計於2026年底完成；
▪於2025年第一季完成Hawaii旅館的客房翻修與客房轉換計畫，總計近75百萬美元，第二階段及最終階段的客房翻修與轉換計畫將於Hilton Waikoloa Village進行
於 2026 年 1 月完成，第二階段且為最後一階段於希爾頓夏威夷村威基基海灘度假村預計於 2026 年 3 月完成，總計約 85 百萬美元用於兩間酒店；以及
◦ 超過 100 百萬美元的全面翻新工程於皇家棕櫚南灘邁阿密，為希爾頓致敬系列度假村，該翻新工程於 2025 年 5 月啟動，包含於海灘酒店翻新所有 393 間客房，並新增 11 間客房，預計於 2026 年 6 月重新開幕。
我們亦可能透過重新定位某些核心酒店於不同品牌或連鎖規模分部，以及探索適應性再利用機會，以確保我們的資產達到其最佳使用效益。最後，我們致力於維持我們核心酒店的競爭力，並透過翻新酒店以符合演變中的顧客偏好，提供更新的客房設計、開放且活躍的 lobby 區域、餐飲與公共空間，以及現代化的會議空間。

• 透過謹慎的資本配置追求成長與多元化。我們意圖利用我們的規模、流動性與交易專業知識，在旅館週期的各個階段創造價值，透過機會性的收購、出售或企業交易，以及在核心酒店內進行價值提升的投資項目，我們相信這將使我們進一步多元化資產組合。自 2017 年 1 月 3 日從希爾頓母公司分拆，成為獨立上市的公司以來，我們已出售或以其他方式處置 51 間酒店，大多位於低成長的國內與國際市場，總計達 3 十億美元，這為我們提供了額外的流動性以減少資產負債表的負債，並執行多種戰略企業計畫。此外，我們持續進行出售我們剩餘非核心酒店的進展。我們將持續機會性地擴大我們在目標市場的佔有率，並隨時間進一步多元化，包括在適當的情況下收購與領先酒店品牌與經營者相關的酒店。

• 維持強而有彈性的資產負債表。我們意圖維持強而有彈性的資產負債表，以應對旅館週期的各個季節。我們預期維持足夠的流動性，並保持短週期到期的債務為最小，並意圖擁有混合型的債務，以提供我們在需要時預先償還債務、出售非核心酒店、執行我們在現有核心資產組合內的價值提升策略，以及支持收購活動的靈活性。2025 年 9 月，本公司與我們的營運公司簽訂了第二修正並重述的信貸協議（"信貸協議"），該協議為高收益無擔保週轉信貸設施（"週轉信貸"）的總承諾額從 950 百萬美元增至 1 十億美元，新增 800 百萬美元高收益無擔保延後提款貸款設施（"2025 延後提款貸款"），該貸款允許至 2026 年 9 月 17 日為止進行最多三次提款，並持續 200 百萬美元高收益無擔保貸款（"2024 貸款"）。信貸協議包含增加週轉信貸與增加或新增貸款設施的選擇權，總額最多可增加 1 十億美元，但需取得額外貸款人承諾並符合某些慣例條件。我們預期會隨著時間減少我們的擔保債務，因為我們意圖在 2026 年透過 2025 延後提款貸款提款，以協助償還兩筆總計約 1.4 十億美元到期於 2026 年的抵押貸款。我們也意圖透過出售我們非核心酒店的所得進一步償還債務，這將提供額外的資產負債表靈活性。我們的高階管理團隊擁有廣泛的經驗管理多個旅館週期的資本結構，並與許多貸款機構與財務顧問有長期且穩固的關係，以應對我們的資本需求。
以下表格提供截至 2026 年 2 月 20 日我們資產組合的總結資訊。

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應配合附屬財務報表、相關附註及本年度10-K申報表第1A項「風險因素」一併閱讀。有關2023年度財務狀況及營運成果與2024年度之比較，請參閱本年度10-K申報表第7項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」。

我們擁有涵蓋知名且市場領先的飯店與度假村的多樣化投資組合，並具有顯著的不動產價值。目前我們持有34間飯店的權益，包含高階品牌飯店與度假村，約有23,000間客房，位於美國主要市場及其屬地。我們的戰略重點為核心組合，我們合併核心飯店約貢獻90%的飯店調整後營業利益。我們核心組閤中超過96%的客房為豪華與上檔次，核心飯店位於主要都會與會議地區，例如紐約市、華盛頓特區、芝加哥、波士頓、紐奧良與丹佛；以及重點休閒目的地的頂級度假村，包括夏威夷、奧蘭多、基韋士堡與邁阿密海灘；以及部分機場與郊區的飯店。

我們的目標是成為首屈一指的住宿不動產投資信託（"REIT"），透過積極的資產管理與深思熟慮的外部成長策略，持續為股東提供優秀且風險調整後的回報，同時維持強而有彈性的資產負債表。作為一家純粹的不動產公司，擁有直接取得資金與獨立財務資源的優勢，我們相信我們強化執行具吸引力的投資回報計畫的能力，代表重要的內生成長機會，特別是針對我們的核心組合。最後，基於我們的規模與投資專業知識，我們相信我們將能成功執行單一資產與組合收購，並處分所有13間非核心飯店，以進一步提升我們資產價值與多元化程度，於住宿產業週期中持續增強。
由於我們業務策略的轉變，即處分所有非核心飯店，我們現今透過三個營運部門運作業務，即合併核心飯店、合併非核心飯店與未合併飯店。僅合併核心飯店與合併非核心飯店為應報告分部。有關我們營運部門的更多資訊，請參閱本年度10-K申報表中附屬審計財務報表的第14項「營運部門資訊」。
合併財務報表依照美國通用會計準則（"U.S. GAAP"）編製，反映我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流。有關更多資訊，請參閱本年度10-K申報表中附屬審計財務報表的第2項「財務報表編製基礎與重要會計政策摘要」。

經濟動盪，包括因利率與通貨膨脹率升高所導致的影響，可能不利於我們的業務，影響消費者情緒與旅遊需求。持續的貿易政策、稅收政策變動與政府支出中斷所造成的不確定性，已導致通貨膨脹擔憂與需求與旅遊偏好變動，可能影響住宿產業。此外，地緣政治衝突與趨勢可能持續減少國際入境旅遊。2025年，我們依賴飯店表現與積極資產管理來緩解目前總體經濟的不確定性。雖然無法保證我們不會因通貨膨脹及其他總體經濟因素、地方經濟因素與需求，潛在經濟放緩或衰退、地緣政治衝突或趨勢、對美國外國或國內政策的不滿，或另一場政府停擺而導致飯店收入或營收進一步波動，但我們對2026年持謹慎樂觀的態度，基於即將到來的重大事件，包括世界盃與美國250週年紀念，持續受益於部分飯店的轉型翻新，包括預計於2026年6月重開的邁阿密皇家棕櫚南灘飯店（"皇家棕櫚"），為Tribute Portfolio度假村，以及處分非核心飯店的效益與持續放鬆管制預期的總體經濟改善。

我們飯店的收入主要來自兩類客戶：散客與團體，歷史來看，這兩類客戶約分別佔我們客房收入的三分之二與三分之一。散客為為商務或休閒目的而旅行的個人旅客。團體客戶為為舉辦會議、研討會或社交活動而預訂客房的團體，由協會、企業、社交、軍事、教育、宗教或其他組織所舉辦。團體業務通常包括一塊客房住宿，以及其他附屬服務，例如會議設施、餐飲與宴會服務。我們大部分的餐飲與其他附屬服務銷售，是由同時入住我們飯店的客戶所產生。因此，入住率會影響我們飯店所有收入組成部分。
客房。代表我們飯店客房出租的銷售，並佔我們總收入的絕大多數。
餐飲業。代表來自集團功能的收入，可能包括婚宴收入及音響視訊收入，以及來自我們飯店內外場餐廳及休閒區的收入。
附屬飯店。代表在飯店內為旅客提供的服務收入，包括停車場、電信業者、高爾夫球場及水療服務。亦包含租賃收入及其它租賃收入。
其他。主要與我們為HGV分時度假產業所提供的支援服務有關，這些產業位於或鄰近我們的飯店，包含提供客房清潔、園藝、一般維護及其他服務的成本補償費用，加上代表成本補償費用百分比的費用。

消費者需求。我們產品及服務的消費者需求與總體經濟表現密切相關，並對企業及個人的非必要開支水準敏感。需求的領先指標包括國內生產總值、非住宅固定投資及消費者物價指數。因總體經濟條件惡化、旅遊模式減少、消費者信心下降、疫情或傳染病爆發，以及政治條件不利等因素，可能降低我們飯店的收入與獲利能力。此外，對旅客的競爭及我們飯店服務的供給，會影響我們維持或提高對旅客收費的能力。因此，消費者需求的變化及總體經濟週期的變動，過去已造成並可能在未來對我們的收入產生顯著波動。另外，目前我們的過夜旅客需求中，休閒旅客佔大多數。因此，我們將比商務旅遊趨勢更受休閒旅遊趨勢的影響。
供給。新客房供給是影響旅館業表現的重要因素。當需求成長超過供給成長時，房價與入住率，以及因此產生的每間可用客房收入（RevPAR），傾向於上升。新競爭力飯店及度假村的增加，會影響現有飯店及度假村維持或成長RevPAR的能力，進而影響獲利。
客房。這些成本包括客房清潔、預訂系統、客房用品、飯店洗衣服務及櫃臺成本。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們面臨因收購活動而產生的各種風險。
與我們現有及未來第三方飯店經理及特許經營商之間的契約或其他爭議，可能使我們對他們負有責任，或導致訴訟費用或其他費用。
根據某些新的非所得稅法規則及規範，我們可能被視為與第三方飯店經理為共同僱主。
針對我們飯店經理或我們自身資訊科技及系統，包括第三方服務供應商的網路威脅及網路安全事件風險，可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
與品牌營運標準相關的成本或未能維持該標準，可能對我們的營運成果及獲利造成重大且不利的影響。
如果我們所投保的保險無法充分覆蓋涉及我們資產的損壞或其他潛在損失或責任，包括因恐怖主義及氣候變遷所致，我們的利潤可能減少。
我們有投資於合資項目，這會限制我們管理這些項目相關第三方風險的能力。
我們依賴外部資金來源以支應未來成長。任何對我們在特定時點及條件上取得資金的能力造成中斷，可能對我們的業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
若我們被判定違反基地租賃契約或無法續約基地租賃契約，可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
與我們產業相關的風險
我們所處的產業為高度競爭的產業。
旅館產業受季節性波動影響，預期會對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成波動。
政府規範可能對我們的不動產及本公司整體營運產生不利影響。
與我們負債相關的風險
與本公司 REIT 狀態及某些其他稅務項目相關的風險
若本公司無法維持符合 REIT 的資格，將被視為 C 董事會公司並需納稅，可能會面臨重大稅務負擔。
本公司可能面臨其他稅務負擔，導致現金流減少。
符合 REIT 要求可能迫使本公司借款以向股東發放紅利。
本公司與 TRS 之間的交易，若未以公平交易條件進行，可能會導致本公司就某些所得或扣除額面臨 100% 的罰稅。
若本公司飯店與 TRS 租賃方之間的租賃關係，在美國聯邦所得稅目的上未被視為真實租賃，將導致本公司無法符合 REIT 的資格。
paragraphs: 持有本公司普通股涉及許多重大風險。您應謹慎考慮下列風險因素。若任何下列風險，以及目前尚未知悉或本公司認為不重要之其他風險與不確定性發生，將可能對本公司之業務、流動性、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大且不利之影響。若發生此種情況，本公司普通股之市場價格可能大幅下跌，您可能喪失全部或部分對本公司普通股之投資價值。此外，下列風險因素中之陳述包含前瞻性聲明。請參閱『前瞻性聲明』。
經濟動盪，包括因通貨膨脹、利率升高或經濟減速或衰退所產生之影響，可能對本公司之業務、財務表現與狀況、營運成果與現金流造成不利影響與幹擾。

經濟動盪，包括因利率升高與通貨膨脹率升高或潛在經濟減速或衰退所產生之影響，可能透過影響消費者情緒與旅遊需求，對本公司業務造成不利影響，進而導致本公司飯店之收入或獲利出現波動。本公司之勞動成本或其他成本亦可能因通貨膨脹而上升，且無法保證本公司能將成本增加轉嫁至旅客透過提高房價。此外，亦無法保證本公司未來不會因通貨膨脹及其他總體經濟因素、地方經濟因素與需求、潛在經濟減速或衰退以及地緣政治衝突或趨勢（包括貿易政策、旅遊限制或美國旅遊目的地之旅遊偏好變動）而導致本公司飯店之收入或獲利出現波動。
此外，全球 COVID-19 疫情對飯店業之影響前所未見，未來若發生另一場疫情或其他未預期事件，導致旅遊人數持續減少，可能產生類似影響，包括全球旅館需求大幅減少與歷史性低佔用率。這些挑戰可能對本公司之業務、財務表現與狀況、營運成果與現金流造成不利影響與幹擾。
其他可能對本公司成功營運造成負面影響，或可能以其他方式對本公司之業務、財務表現與狀況、營運成果與現金流造成重大且不利影響與幹擾的因素包括：
•持續負面之消費者或企業情緒、經濟指標（包括通貨膨脹、失業率、可支配支出與個人財富減少）或旅遊需求，可能進一步對旅館需求造成不利影響；
